source: Miller Millermatic 252 Owner's Manual: section 6-5 Troubleshooting (printed p. 31, 5 troubles -> 21 remedy rows; no cause column, so each row key is its remedy text), sections 8-8 to 8-15 (printed pp. 41-43, 8 defects -> 22 cause rows), section 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment (printed pp. 44-45, 4 problems -> 20 cause rows). Deterministic parser output: 17 symptoms -> 63 cause rows.
scope_disclaimer: The oracle proves the twin matches the manual's claims, not that the machine behaves that way. Field data is the only real ground truth.

review.note: Written once, per case, as a separate reviewed artifact from any twin or archetype (OMNIPRO oracle method, Phase 3A). The vocabulary author writes the expected vectors from the manual pages only. Rows flagged in 'flags' are vocabulary-author judgement where the manual is silent or covers two directions in one cause row; those flags are the reviewer's starting point. The corrective-action column is held out in 'answer_key' and must never be sent to the system under test. 27 Nov 2026 injection/vocabulary update (proof-twin measurement, 0/38 run): miller-01 fault is now fault/stuck_open and miller-02 fault/tripped (the switch archetype treats state as an output the nominal row overwrites; fault is its input channel); miller-52 fault is now level/empty (empty is the storage level parameter, as in OMNIPRO); fan values are normalised to the twin motion_out domain (running->normal, stopped->absent).

join_rule: A vocabulary row joins to a deterministic-parser cause row on row_id (stable parser output: tools/parse_welder_oracles.py). Cause text is the parser's exact text. The remedy is NOT carried on the row: it is the held-out answer key.

categories.twin_expressible: Fault injection on an archetype fault state or a parameter value. The scored headline set.
categories.settings: A setting / configuration value, not a fault injection. Recorded with its expected vector, not scored as a fault row.
categories.technique: Technique / contamination. Not twin-expressible. Own category, not scored.
categories.cross_reference: Routes to another case; counted once, under that case.
categories.unmappable: States no diagnosable cause at all (a safety stop, not a fault). Recorded, not scored.

disconnect_check.description: Line disconnect switch On (6-5: 'Be sure line disconnect switch is On').

breaker_check.description: Building line fuse / circuit breaker not open (6-5).

trigger_check.description: Gun trigger connections secure; trigger not faulty or shorted (6-5).

power_cycle_check.description: Turn power switch off and back on; meter message clears or reappears (6-5, HL.P 001).

board_check.description: Board connections / main control board sound (6-5: Factory Authorized Service Agent check). A service-agent check, not an operator check.

ground_check.description: Work clamp metal-to-metal contact (6-5: 'Connect work clamp to get good metal to metal contact').

tip_condition_check.description: Contact tip condition (6-5: replace contact tip).

input_voltage_check.description: Unit connected to proper input voltage; line voltage not low; primary voltage correct (6-5; 8-17).

jumper_link_check.description: Input voltage jumper links in the correct position (6-5; sections 4-11).

liner_tip_check.description: Inlet guide, contact tip, liner sound (6-5).

voltage_setting_check.description: Voltage range / voltage setting for the selected wire feed speed (8-8; 8-17).

stickout_check.description: Electrode extension (stickout) / wire extension beyond nozzle, not more than 1/2 in (13 mm) (8-8; 8-9; 8-14).

workpiece_clean_check.description: Work surface free of grease, oil, moisture, rust, paint, coatings and dirt (8-8; 8-9; 8-12).

wire_clean_check.description: Welding wire clean and dry, no oil/lubricant pickup from feeder or liner (8-8; 8-9).

gas_flow_check.description: Shielding gas flow at the welding arc (8-8; 8-9).

gas_type_check.description: Welding grade shielding gas, correct gas for the job (8-9).

heat_input_check.description: Heat input: voltage range and wire feed speed, travel speed (8-10 to 8-13; 8-15).

joint_prep_check.description: Joint preparation and design give access to the bottom of the groove (8-11).

technique_check.description: Welding technique: gun angle 0-15 degrees, arc on leading edge, hand steadiness, bead placement (8-11; 8-12; 8-14).

gun_restriction_check.description: Restriction in the gun and/or assembly: cable, gun, contact tip (8-17).

liner_tip_size_check.description: Cable liner and gun contact tip size match the wire (8-17).

connector_seated_check.description: Gun end inserted into the drive housing properly (8-17).

gas_valve_check.description: Gas cylinder valve open, flowmeter adjusted (8-17).

gas_line_check.description: Gas hose between flowmeter and wire feeder, and in the gun and cable assembly, clear (8-17).

solenoid_check.description: Gas solenoid wiring and valve operating (8-17).

cable_connection_check.description: Connections at the gun weld cable and work cable tight (8-17, arc not stable).

gun_condition_check.description: Gun in good shape, no loose connection inside the gun (8-17, arc not stable).

miller-01.cause: Be sure line disconnect switch is On (see Section 4-13).
miller-01.corrective_action: Be sure line disconnect switch is On (see Section 4-13).

miller-02.cause: Replace building line fuse or reset circuit breaker if open (see Section 4-13).
miller-02.corrective_action: Replace building line fuse or reset circuit breaker if open (see Section 4-13).

miller-03.cause: Secure gun trigger connections (see welding gun Owner’s Manual).
miller-03.corrective_action: Secure gun trigger connections (see welding gun Owner’s Manual).

miller-04.cause: HL.P 001 appears on meters. Turn power switch off and back on, if HL.P 001 appears on meters again, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check unit.
miller-04.corrective_action: HL.P 001 appears on meters. Turn power switch off and back on, if HL.P 001 appears on meters again, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check unit.

miller-05.cause: HL.P 002 appears on meters. Thermistor T is detecting an overheating condition. Wait for unit to cool allowing the fan to run. After unit is cool, if HL.P 002 message remains, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check for an open Thermistor T (see Section 6-2).
miller-05.corrective_action: HL.P 002 appears on meters. Thermistor T is detecting an overheating condition. Wait for unit to cool allowing the fan to run. After unit is cool, if HL.P 002 message remains, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check for an open Thermistor T (see Section 6-2).

miller-06.cause: HL.P 004 appears on meters. Reset message by releasing the trigger or removing stuck wire causing short circuit (see Section 5-2) . If message remains, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check for shorted trigger leads.
miller-06.corrective_action: HL.P 004 appears on meters. Reset message by releasing the trigger or removing stuck wire causing short circuit (see Section 5-2) . If message remains, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check for shorted trigger leads.

miller-07.cause: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check Power switch.
miller-07.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check Power switch.

miller-08.cause: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check all board connections and main control board.
miller-08.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check all board connections and main control board.

miller-09.cause: Connect work clamp to get good metal to metal contact.
miller-09.corrective_action: Connect work clamp to get good metal to metal contact.

miller-10.cause: Replace contact tip (see welding gun Owner’s Manual.
miller-10.corrective_action: Replace contact tip (see welding gun Owner’s Manual.

miller-11.cause: HL.P 003 appears on meters, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board and main rectifier.
miller-11.corrective_action: HL.P 003 appears on meters, have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board and main rectifier.

miller-12.cause: Connect unit to proper input voltage or check for low line voltage (see Section 4-13).
miller-12.corrective_action: Connect unit to proper input voltage or check for low line voltage (see Section 4-13).

miller-13.cause: Check input voltage jumper links and correct position if necessary (see Section 4-11).
miller-13.corrective_action: Check input voltage jumper links and correct position if necessary (see Section 4-11).

miller-14.cause: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.
miller-14.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.

miller-15.cause: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check fan-on-demand circuit.
miller-15.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check fan-on-demand circuit.

miller-17.cause: Change to correct size drive rolls (see Section 6-3).
miller-17.corrective_action: Change to correct size drive rolls (see Section 6-3).

miller-19.cause: Replace inlet guide, contact tip, and/or liner if necessary (see welding gun Owner’s Manual).
miller-19.corrective_action: Replace inlet guide, contact tip, and/or liner if necessary (see welding gun Owner’s Manual).

miller-20.cause: Check position of input jumper links (see Section 4-11).
miller-20.corrective_action: Check position of input jumper links (see Section 4-11).

miller-21.cause: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.
miller-21.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.

miller-25.corrective_action: Remove all grease, oil, moisture, rust, paint, undercoating, and dirt from work surface before welding.

miller-26.cause: Insufficient shielding gas at welding arc.
miller-26.corrective_action: Increase flow of shielding gas at regulator/flowmeter and/or prevent drafts near welding arc.

miller-27.corrective_action: Use clean, dry welding wire. Eliminate pickup of oil or lubricant on welding wire from feeder or liner.

miller-28.cause: Insufficient shielding gas at welding arc.
miller-28.corrective_action: Increase flow of shielding gas at regulator/flowmeter and/or prevent drafts near welding arc. Remove spatter from gun nozzle. Check gas hoses for leaks. Place nozzle 1/4 to 1/2 in (6-13 mm) from workpiece. Hold gun near bead at end of weld until molten metal solidifies.

miller-29.corrective_action: Use welding grade shielding gas; change to different gas.

miller-30.corrective_action: Use clean, dry welding wire. Eliminate pick up of oil or lubricant on welding wire from feeder or liner.

miller-31.corrective_action: Remove all grease, oil, moisture, rust, paint, coatings, and dirt from work surface before welding. Use a more highly deoxidizing welding wire (contact supplier).

miller-32.cause: Welding wire extends too far out of nozzle.
miller-32.corrective_action: Be sure welding wire extends not more than 1/2 in (13 mm) beyond nozzle.

miller-33.corrective_action: Select lower voltage range and reduce wire feed speed. Increase travel speed.

miller-34.corrective_action: Material too thick. Joint preparation and design must provide access to bottom of groove while maintaining proper welding wire extension and arc characteristics.

miller-35.corrective_action: Maintain normal gun angle of 0 to 15 degrees to achieve maximum penetration. Keep arc on leading edge of weld puddle. Be sure welding wire extends not more than 1/2 in (13 mm) beyond nozzle.

miller-36.corrective_action: Select higher wire feed speed and/or select higher voltage range. Reduce travel speed.

miller-37.corrective_action: Remove all grease, oil, moisture, rust, paint, undercoating, and dirt from work surface before welding.

miller-38.corrective_action: Select higher voltage range and/or adjust wire feed speed.

miller-39.corrective_action: Place stringer bead in proper location(s) at joint during welding. Adjust work angle or widen groove to access bottom during welding. Momentarily hold arc on groove side walls when using weaving technique. Keep arc on leading edge of weld puddle. Use correct gun angle of 0 to 15 degrees.

miller-40.corrective_action: Select lower voltage range and reduce wire feed speed. Increase and/or maintain steady travel speed.

miller-41.cause: Welding wire extends too far out of nozzle.
miller-41.corrective_action: Be sure welding wire extends not more than 1/2 in (13 mm) beyond nozzle.

miller-42.corrective_action: Support hand on solid surface or use two hands.

miller-43.corrective_action: Use restraint (clamp) to hold base metal in position. Make tack welds along joint before starting welding operation. Select lower voltage range and/or reduce wire feed speed. Increase travel speed. Weld in small segments and allow cooling between welds.

miller-44.cause: Too little pressure on wire feed rolls.
miller-44.corrective_action: Increase pressure setting on wire feed rolls.
miller-44.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-45.corrective_action: Check size stamped on wire feed rolls, replace to match wire size and type if necessary.
miller-45.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-46.cause: Wire spool brake pressure too high.
miller-46.corrective_action: Decrease brake pressure on wire spool.
miller-46.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-47.cause: Restriction in the gun and/or assembly.
miller-47.corrective_action: Check and replace cable, gun, and contact tip if damaged. Check size of contact tip and cable liner, replace if necessary.
miller-47.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-48.cause: Too much pressure on wire feed rolls.
miller-48.corrective_action: Decrease pressure setting on wire feed rolls.
miller-48.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-49.cause: Incorrect cable liner or gun contact tip size.
miller-49.corrective_action: Check size of contact tip and check cable liner length and diameter, replace if necessary.
miller-49.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-50.cause: Gun end not inserted into drive housing properly.
miller-50.corrective_action: Loosen gun securing bolt in drive housing and push gun end into housing just enough so it does not touch wire feed rolls.
miller-50.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-54.corrective_action: Open gas valve at cylinder and adjust flow rate.
miller-54.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-55.corrective_action: Check gas hose between flowmeter and wire feeder, and gas hose in gun and cable assembly.
miller-55.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-56.cause: Loose or broken wires to gas solenoid.
miller-56.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent repair wiring.
miller-56.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-57.corrective_action: Have Factory Authorized Service Agent replace gas solenoid valve.
miller-57.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-58.cause: Incorrect primary voltage connected to welding power source.
miller-58.corrective_action: Check primary voltage and relink welding power source for correct voltage.
miller-58.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-59.corrective_action: Adjust pressure setting on wire feed rolls. Replace worn drive rolls if necessary.
miller-59.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment

miller-60.cause: Wrong size gun liner or contact tip.
miller-60.corrective_action: Match liner and contact tip to wire size and type.

miller-61.source_table: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide for Semiautomatic Welding Equipment
